ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A park is shaped like an equilateral triangle. A cat wants to walk along one of the three indicated paths (thicker lines) from the upper corner to the lower right corner. The lengths of the paths are $P, Q$ and $R$, as shown. Which of the following statements about the lengths of the paths is true?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image there are three triangular paths of the same shape, respectively labeled P, Q, R. Each thick black path is composed of several slanted side segments and three horizontal segments; dashed horizontal auxiliary lines mark the same height levels: from top to bottom they can be denoted as A, B, C, D. The lower the horizontal secant is, the longer it is, so A < B < C < D. When reasoning, regard the three outer triangles as similar and with the same slanted-side slope. The slanted-side parts of each path together all descend from the vertex to the base, so the total slanted-side lengths of the three paths are the same. Thus it is only necessary to compare the total lengths of the three horizontal segments. From the figure it can be read: P uses horizontal segments at levels A, B, D; R uses horizontal segments at levels A, C, D; Q uses horizontal segments at levels B, C, D. Therefore P = A+B+D, R = A+C+D, Q = B+C+D. Because A < B < C, P < R < Q.

raw_record.question_text: In the diagram, order the three indicated path lengths P, Q, and R from shortest to longest.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: each labeled path P, Q, and R is a broken path on a triangular figure, made of slanted side segments plus three horizontal segments. The dotted horizontal guide lines show that the corresponding heights are shared across the three triangles: upper level A, middle level B, lower level C, and base level D. Treat the three outer triangles as similar with the same side slopes, so a horizontal cross-section gets longer the lower it is. Then reason: for each path, the slanted pieces together descend from the apex to the base, so their total slanted length is the same for P, Q, and R. The ordering is therefore determined only by the total horizontal distance. Read the horizontals as P using levels A, B, D; R using A, C, D; and Q using B, C, D. Since widths increase downward, A < B < C < D, giving P = A+B+D, R = A+C+D, Q = B+C+D. Hence P < R < Q.
